stories.topic: Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
stories.text: Five Palestinians are killed, including a child, and others are injured in a series of Israeli airstrikes on various areas of the Gaza Strip, Palestine.

stories.topic: Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war, Israeli settler violence
stories.text: A 72-year-old Palestinian woman is killed and ten others are injured in an attack by Israeli settlers on Palestinian homes in the village of Ein ad-Duyuk at-Tahta west of Jericho in the occupied West Bank.
Bahrain's military intercepts a number of drones fired by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) at Sheikh Isa Air Base.
The United States Air Force conducts a series of at least six strikes on Qeshm Island. The IRGC says it shot down a General Atomics MQ-9 Reaper drone south of the island.

The Crimean Bridge is struck by Ukrainian drones for the second day in a row, killing two people and prompting Russian authorities to close vehicle traffic again. Open-source intelligence report that a section of the road bridge damaged yesterday has collapsed into the Kerch Strait.

Following the arrest of party leaders, banned Awami League and Chhatra League activists mobilize via mosque loudspeakers to storm and burn a police station in Tungipara, Gopalganj District, Bangladesh. Amid police tear gas and rubber bullet fire, the attackers free detainees, loot firearms, burn Bangladesh Nationalist Party MP S M Jilani's (Gopalganj-3) residence, and blockade local roads.
In Comilla, Bangladesh, Swechhasebak Dal members burn the local Awami League office and former MP AKM Bahauddin Bahar's residence in retaliation for the attack on BNP leader S M Jilani's home.

Bangladeshi police and 42 platoons of the Border Guard Bangladesh deploy tear gas, stun grenades, batons, and surveillance drones against garment workers across Dhaka, Savar, Ashulia, Gazipur, and Narayanganj protesting for a minimum wage hike from ৳12,500 (US$100) to ৳30,000 ($240). Protesters block the N3, N4, and N5 highways and shutter 37 factories after a Minimum Wage Board meeting is delayed to November 23.

Canada and China agree to further tariff reductions following talks between Canadian prime minister Mark Carney and Chinese leader Xi Jinping before the APEC summit in Shenzhen. China reduces tariffs on C$400 million (¥1.8 billion) in Canadian exports, while Canada extends relief for Chinese steel and aluminium.

stories.topic: 2026 Russian Air Force Antonov An-12 crash
stories.text: A Russian Air Force Antonov An-12 crashes near Kemerovo, Russia, killing all 19 people on board.
Forty-six people are injured after a collision between two trains in Prague, Czech Republic.

The Pan American Health Organization revokes the measles elimination statuses of Bolivia, Mexico, and the United States. For the U.S., the organization cited continuous domestic transmission for over 12 months amid more than 5,700 reported infections and multiple deaths in 2026.

France and Malaysia establish a strategic partnership, signing agreements on defence, energy, and technology cooperation during French president Emmanuel Macron's state visit. Malaysia also agrees to permit limited exports of unprocessed rare-earth minerals to France in exchange for assistance with mineral processing.

stories.topic: Israel–United Kingdom relations, United Kingdom and the Gaza war
stories.text: British foreign secretary Ed Miliband announces that the United Kingdom will sanction eight companies involved in the construction of settlements in the occupied West Bank, as well as Tzav 9 for its role in blocking humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip.
Investigative journalist Camilo Rodríguez is shot dead in his vehicle in Santo Domingo, Heredia, Costa Rica, in the first journalist death in the country in at least 25 years.
A factory worker is hacked to death after filming clashes between two factions of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party in Fatullah, Narayanganj District.

A court in Conakry, Guinea, tries over 1,000 alleged artisanal gold miners for illegal gold mining in the Siguiri region, resulting in the sentencing of 22 former regional administrators and 202 others to various prison terms.

The North Macedonian Agency for National Security arrests five Macedonian nationals allegedly linked to an assassination plot in Greece, allegedly involving Iranian recruiters, including Naji Sharifi-Zindashti, who is wanted by the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation. A sixth person remains at large. Greek public television reports that the target was a Israeli business executive based in Athens.

Mongolian president Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh announces his resignation from office, three days after former Ulaanbaatar mayor Khishgeegiin Nyambaatar accused him of past embezzlement from a railway project during his tenure as prime minister. The State Great Khural must accept the resignation for it to become effective.

stories.topic: Haitian crisis, Salvadoran military intervention in Haiti
stories.text: Hundreds of Haitians march in cities across Haiti to show support for the deployment of Salvadoran troops to combat gang violence.

American technology company Apple experiences an outage with several of its services, including Apple Pay, iCloud, the App Store, and AppleCare. The company's spokesperson attributed the problems to an internal update and rules out a cyberattack.
Racing NSW launches an investigation after the body of losing horse So You Are is found in a skip bin in Sydney, Australia.
